note: Quote verbatim on p. 29. Officials named by office. The paper’s quoted words "enhance transparency, credibility and public trust" are paraphrased without quotation marks ("add to"), because "enhance" is on the site’s banned list and check_writing.py reads the event text.
final_text: The Commission launched ECINet, bringing more than 40 of its apps and portals, the roll software among them, onto one platform. The Chief Election Commissioner said it was built in strict accordance with the law, and the Director General of IT said it would add to transparency, credibility and public trust.

note: Quote verbatim on p. 33. Text says no more than the quote ("for notices and hearings" restored to the paper’s "for issuing notices and holding hearings").
final_text: With the revision under way in 12 states and union territories, and the IT division moving registration officers onto a new module for issuing notices and holding hearings, Sanjay Kumar asked the Director General of IT to make sure the system did not restrict a registration officer’s discretion.

note: Quote verbatim across pp. 53 to 54 (a cartoon caption interrupts p. 53). "wrote that day" followed a sentence about 22 January and could be read as that date, so the 11 February date is stated. "The Indian Express reported" dropped as redundant: every entry in the section is the paper’s account.
final_text: Goa’s registration officers had heard 649 flagged electors and found 97 eligible, but ECINet had no way to reverse their earlier entries. Requests for that option had been coming from the field since 22 January. On 11 February Goa Electronics Limited, the state agency that supports the Chief Electoral Officer’s office on the software, wrote to the Chief Electoral Officer and to Tata Consultancy Services, the Commission’s vendor. The Chief Electoral Officer forwarded the complaint the same day to the Senior Deputy Election Commissioner in charge of Goa, copied to the Director General of IT.

note: Quote verbatim on pp. 33 to 34, in the ECINet article (the event links the 14-objections article, which carries the first half; a second research row records the ECINet article for the added half). "all necessary approvals" put in quotation marks as the paper prints it.
final_text: Sandhu recorded that communications were going out in the Commission’s name without its approval, and that the IT division had built new modules and portals that were never put to him or to the Commission. He wrote that he had learnt of them from the media, and asked that the Director General of IT be directed to keep every member of the Commission briefed and to obtain “all necessary approvals” before any new work.

note: Quote verbatim on p. 34. The proposal placed the IIT expert inside the first committee, which the paper does not say in terms. The text now keeps the paper’s order (an audit with an expert from the IITs, then the two checks) and its "had the credentials".
final_text: Joshi wrote of the “gradual centralisation of the electoral roll database” and proposed an audit, with an outside expert from the IITs. One committee would review the systems from time to time and certify that only the statutory officers had the credentials to change the voter database. A second would check whether ECINet complied with the law and see that any change of policy or procedure in ERONet and ECINet was brought before the Commission.

note: Quote verbatim on p. 26, which also supports "on the portal". The rest of the sentence was already in the entry.
final_text: In a note to the Deputy Election Commissioner and the Director General in charge of IT, copied to the Chief Election Commissioner and Joshi, Sandhu wrote that the change to the online Form 6 was “unauthorised/illegal” and must be taken off the portal at once so that eligible first-time voters could register without harassment.

note: Quote verbatim on p. 38. Text says no more than the quote.
final_text: Sandhu recorded that Chief Electoral Officers, district officers and registration officers had told him they lacked proper and complete access to ERONet, that access control had been centralised at the level of the Director General of IT, and that the Director General of IT had no legal authority to restrict them. He directed that full access be given at once, and asked the Director General of IT to certify, on confirmations from every Chief Electoral Officer, that the statutory officers in all states and union territories had full access. He added that he knew of no action on the audit notes.

note: Quote verbatim across pp. 50 to 51. Not added as a new event: the paper does not date the questionnaire, so a separate entry dated 24 September would assert a date the source does not give, and a new entry would renumber the three that follow. Appended to "The Goa account is published", the alternative the first reader offered.
final_text: The Indian Express published the eight messages from Goa and the 97 electors left off its final roll. The paper said it had asked the Director General of IT, who heads the Commission’s IT division, why the rollback option was not enabled for Goa before the final roll, and had no response.

note: Both flexibility quotes verbatim (pp. 60 and 69), and p. 59 to 60 attribute them to the four-page note, so the first sentence is kept. The second sentence ("The Indian Express reported that the note did not explain why the rollback option Goa asked for was never enabled", p. 62) is left out of this entry: it links to the Commission’s own press note, which the section note says carries the Commission’s words, and the paper’s comment is already on the process page in the reported press list for the same article. Agreed with the first reader to leave out the line on whether officers stay.
final_text: After its meeting, the Commission’s press note 120 listed nine decisions. Documents to be collected at home from those sent notices, help desks and camps for the homeless and the poor, the statutory Form 6 outside the revision, a review of ECINet by a committee with an IIT or IIIT expert and new IT modules to go through a committee of officers, later dates in Delhi and Maharashtra, agendas and minutes for every meeting, appraisal reports on time, the Commission’s approval for officers’ foreign trips, and Commissioners’ directions to be complied with. It ordered a special drive to enrol those left out, said the letter to the Cabinet Secretary concerned an officer on deputation whose reallocation of work was never put into effect, and said 81 of Goa’s 97 had filled in Form 6. The note also said that any further flexibility field officers needed in the software would be made operational.

note: Quote verbatim on p. 69. The paper’s quoted words are kept in quotation marks.
final_text: A letter from the Commission’s Secretary told the 20 states and union territories where the revision is over to run a special drive to enrol left-out and first-time electors, on the statutory Form 6, and kept the declaration for the revision period only. The letter was copied to the Director General of IT “for making necessary changes in ECINet”.

note: Quotes verbatim on pp. 49 and 32. "By the Express’s account" changed to "By the paper’s account" to match the note, which already names the paper, and ERONet named as ECINet’s roll module as p. 49 does.
final_text: The Indian Express says it has seen these notes and letters. This site has not, and none is public. Every entry below is the paper’s account, linked to its article, except the Commission’s own press notes of 23 and 26 September, which link to the notes. By the paper’s account, what a registration officer can do on ECINet and its roll module, ERONet, is decided by permissions set in the Commission’s IT division in Delhi, headed by the Director General of IT.
